title: Opening the Umbrella: The Effects of Rebranding Multiple Category-Specific Private-Label Brands to One Umbrella Brand
eligible_reason: Although rebranding dates differ across categories, the estimating equation uses matching-based controls, category-specific trends, time-varying marketing-mix controls, treatment-by-covariate interactions, and SUR. None of the reported coefficients is a TWFE or event-study treatment effect.
design_notes: Category-by-category (staggered) rebranding of the private-label tier at two Dutch banners, SPAR (53 categories) and Attent (47 categories), with rebranding dates set by supplier contract end dates; weekly category-level scanner data 2011-2015 (about 129 weeks before and 111 weeks after). Each rebranded category is matched by Mahalanobis distance on 52 pre-period characteristics to the same category at one of seven non-rebranding banners. Eq. 1 is a log-log sales model estimated separately for each category i, with category-specific intercepts, linear and quadratic time trends, own-price/promotion/assortment elasticities (time-varying marketing-mix controls), banner advertising, outlets, consumer confidence, holiday and 4-weekly dummies, and TREAT, POST and TREAT x POST interacted with all of these; jointly estimated with NB and other-PL-tier equations by SUR. Parameters of interest are the category-specific TREAT x POST intercept and elasticity shifts (b_rebr), then aggregated across categories. No unit and calendar-time FE specification; no binary-treatment TWFE coefficient is reported.
screener_notes: Not eligible: matching, category-specific trends, time-varying controls and treatment-by-covariate interactions. No replication package was listed in the batch file (package_dir and regressions_path empty); screening is from the article text only. Retailer store-scanner data from SPAR and Attent, plus GfK household panel and other proprietary retailer data.
